profiles.version_scope: Documentation reviewed 11 October 2026: current Next.js App Router docs label 16.4.0. Pin the installed Next, React, Node and database packages; distinguish cacheComponents:true from the previous caching model. This profile does not qualify a lockfile or hosting adapter.
profiles.operating_model: A Next application contains server rendering and browser interactivity with an explicit trust boundary. Recommendation: preserve an existing backend's domain ownership during UI adoption; for a new owned backend use server-only data access. Node/Docker and alternative adapters require separate runtime checks.
architecture: Server Components load server-owned data; Client Components own interaction and browser APIs. Keep the client boundary near interactive leaves and pass minimal serializable DTOs.

Recommendation: one domain writer and migration owner per responsibility. Existing REST/GraphQL services remain authoritative during coexistence; a new server-only DAL can own validation, authorization and transactions after transfer.

Choose server, browser and CDN caches deliberately. Session-dependent output, invalidation and multiple instances require independent policies; adding a framework cache does not migrate a shared session or queue.
Recommendation: durable jobs and realtime run behind explicit service contracts when required. A render, Server Action or browser promise is not an execution backlog.
developer_workflow: Start in the external source checkout. Read README and inspect package.json, lockfile, next.config, current API ownership, schema and runtime. Record whether Cache Components are enabled before selecting examples.

For an existing npm project run npm ci; use its scripts. With Next installed, npx next typegen then npx tsc --noEmit checks generated route types and TypeScript. Run the configured ESLint/Biome command separately; the build is not a substitute for lint.

Run npm run dev for iteration and npm run build for production compilation; use npm run start only if its script runs the selected production server. Configure Playwright's isolated backend/data first, then npx playwright test for mixed-version journeys.

Recommendation: deploy the same built artifact to all instances, record build/deployment identifiers, cache coordination, migrations, secrets and adapter support. Reproduce cold/warm loads, sign-out, old-tab actions and rollback on a staging topology.
avoid: Marking the root tree use client brings imported dependencies into the browser bundle and broadens the secret/exposure surface.
Passing whole ORM records to Client Components exposes fields unrelated to presentation; enforce authorization and DTO filtering on the server.
UI-hidden buttons or Proxy redirects cannot replace authorization at the mutation/data boundary.
Copying pre-16 cache defaults into a Cache Components app silently changes freshness behavior; identify the installed model.
Treating an old browser build as gone after deployment ignores existing tabs, prefetched payloads and action identifiers.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing REST/GraphQL behavior, DTOs, authorization, transactions and one schema owner.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Adopt server-rendered routes that call the old API; keep its writer and migration authority. Compare read-only fixtures without replaying real side effects.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Retain the API permanently if appropriate, or transfer a bounded domain to a server-only DAL with minimal DTOs after mixed-version checks.

benefits.benefit: Server loading can reduce client waterfalls; an owned DAL centralizes authorization.
benefits.prerequisites: Server-reachable API or reviewed database ownership; measurable user journeys.
benefits.tradeoffs: A new domain writer requires schema/transaction review; framework adoption alone changes neither.

checks: Old and new UI decode identical success/error/empty fixtures.
Forged resource IDs remain denied on both mutation paths.
An acknowledged write is readable through the old interface.
transitions.rollback: Route the cohort back while old-compatible schema remains; reconcile writes before any writer reversal.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing session issuer, cookie/token format, expiry, revocation, tenant membership and CSRF behavior.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Retain the issuer behind an adapter and authorize data/mutations in both implementations; inventory origin/domain/cookie differences before sharing.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use an explicitly selected issuer and server-side authorization boundary; transfer session contracts or require a controlled sign-in when compatibility cannot be preserved.

benefits.benefit: One identity authority can support gradual UI/backend replacement.
benefits.prerequisites: Validated issuer integration and old/new expiry/revocation fixtures.
benefits.tradeoffs: Session sharing is format/security work; sign-in continuity is not guaranteed by using cookies.

checks: Revoked and expired sessions fail in old/new paths.
Cross-tenant direct action requests are denied.
Sign-out clears browser remote-state caches and back navigation reveals no protected data.
transitions.rollback: Restore old routes/issuer acceptance only while its keys and session semantics remain supported; do not resurrect revoked sessions.

transitions.existing_contract: Actual enabled caching model, personalized response policy, keys, freshness, invalidation and shared-instance behavior.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep the prior policy while converting one route/data category; separate old/new cache namespaces and observe stale/account-crossing outcomes.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Choose Cache Components or version-matched previous-model APIs explicitly; keep user-specific data outside shared public entries and coordinate shared invalidation when deployed across instances.

benefits.benefit: Repeated eligible work can be reused without refetching each time.
benefits.prerequisites: A documented freshness tolerance, safe keys and working invalidation.
benefits.tradeoffs: Coordination/storage adds operations; freshness and cost gains require measurement.

checks: A write refreshes affected reads through every serving instance.
Account A cannot read cached output for account B.
Cold, warm and forced-refresh responses agree with the selected policy.
transitions.rollback: Disable the new cache path and purge its namespace; keep source data unchanged and retain old invalidation until transfer completes.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing job producer/consumer payloads, ready/scheduled/retry/failed/in-flight states and external-effect idempotency.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep existing workers; move a named job type behind a versioned event contract. Reconcile backlog and retain one consumer owner per item.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use selected durable execution such as Inngest for required workflows; a transactional outbox is a proposed design when domain commit and event submission are separate systems.

benefits.benefit: Checkpointed completed steps allow retry/resume without starting every step again.
benefits.prerequisites: Selected service/SDK integration, stable step IDs, replay-safe external effects and delivery reconciliation.
benefits.tradeoffs: Operating a workflow service adds dependency/cost; checkpoints do not supply business exactly-once effects.

checks: Crash after an external effect but before step acknowledgement; retry causes one intended business effect.
Domain commit with event-send failure is eventually reconciled.
Old scheduled/retry work is drained or deliberately transformed.
transitions.rollback: Stop new producers for the transferred type, account for active runs and resume old workers with compatible payloads; reconcile irreversible effects first.

transitions.existing_contract: Current hosting/runtime, static assets, open-tab state, prefetched payloads and Server Function compatibility.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep old assets and compatible API routes; promote one built artifact per deployment and rehearse an old tab against the new deployment.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use version-matched deploymentId support and infrastructure routing as needed; same-build instances share required action keys and cache coordination.

benefits.benefit: Explicit rollout handling reduces missing-chunk/navigation mismatches.
benefits.prerequisites: A qualified host, retained assets and tested old-client behavior.
benefits.tradeoffs: Hard navigation can lose component state; same encryption key does not make old action IDs compatible.

checks: Open an old tab, deploy, navigate and submit an old form; observe success or a controlled update path.
Preserved drafts survive any required full reload.
All instances serve matching build/deployment identifiers.
transitions.rollback: Restore the prior artifact and routing while compatible assets/data remain; do not claim traffic rollback reverses schema or external effects.

sources.title: Inngest Durable Execution
sources.claim: Completed steps are checkpointed and workflows can retry/resume; durable endpoints are separately marked beta.

profiles.version_scope: Documentation reviewed 11 October 2026: current React docs label 19.3; current Vite docs include migration from v7 and Rolldown build options. Preserve the project's resolved React/Vite/TypeScript/router versions and API schema. SPA guidance is not a claim that Vite supplies SSR or a backend.
profiles.operating_model: React/Vite builds browser assets. Recommendation: select it when an existing API owns persistence, authorization, email, durable jobs and other privileged effects; choose routing and remote-state tools deliberately. A client-only build has no protected server runtime.
architecture: Views consume route-loaded or query-cached DTOs; one API client module defines credentials, errors, cancellation and runtime validation. Backend ownership remains independent of UI language.
Recommendation: domain state stays on the server; transient form/navigation state stays in the browser. Use tenant-aware cache keys and an explicit account-switch/reset policy.
Bundled VITE_ values are public configuration. Keep database, provider and signing credentials in the backend; a development proxy is only local routing.

Recommendation: retain content-hashed old chunks during rollout, revalidate HTML and provide a guarded update path for stale tabs. Add service-worker storage/adoption policy only if offline operation is required.
developer_workflow: Start at the source README, API schema and lockfile. For a new local prototype npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts creates a starter; record resolved versions before promoting it. Existing applications keep their package manager.

Use npm ci, the configured TypeScript project check (for the standard scaffold npx tsc -b) and npm run build. npm run dev is local development; npm run preview previews a build and is not the production host.
Configure routing, typed API boundaries, TanStack Query only where useful and its QueryClientProvider. Define loading, stale, denied and offline states before using retries.

Recommendation: use browser network/debug tooling and React profiling for the actual slow interaction. Configure Playwright with old/new API fixtures; run npx playwright test only after installing its runner/browsers and setting an isolated webServer.
avoid: Bundling a secret as VITE_API_KEY publishes it to users; moving its string into a frontend module does not create a trust boundary.
Rebuilding server authorization as React route guards allows direct unauthorized API calls.
Independent fetching in nested effects creates waterfalls and duplicated state ownership; use route loaders or a selected remote-state cache where appropriate.
Treating TanStack Query defaults as an application freshness contract overlooks refetch/retry behavior and account boundaries.
Deleting old chunks on deployment breaks lazy imports in open tabs; repeated automatic reload can also discard unsaved work.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing URLs, backend API DTOs, errors, permissions and navigation/deep-link semantics.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Replace one route/screen with React while keeping existing API ownership and deep links; contract fixtures cover old/new UI.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Keep a browser/API split with route loaders or a selected query client; adopt a server framework only when required rendering/backend features justify it.

benefits.benefit: An independently delivered browser client can evolve behind a stable API.
benefits.prerequisites: Owned routing/hosting fallback and backward-compatible API.
benefits.tradeoffs: A SPA must own routing/data/loading infrastructure; SSR/RSC are additional architecture choices.

checks: Direct deep links and refresh work from the production host.
Old/new clients decode success/error/unknown-field fixtures.
Unauthorized direct API requests remain denied.
transitions.rollback: Restore old HTML/assets/routes while API compatibility remains; preserve submitted data and reconcile pending mutations.

transitions.existing_contract: Backend credential transport, allowed origins, cookies/CSRF, token expiry and account boundaries.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep the backend issuer; configure same-origin routing or narrowly allowed credentialed CORS and preserve old clients.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Centralize credential/error behavior in the API client; enforce authorization and any cookie CSRF protection in the backend.

benefits.benefit: One backend authority reduces duplicated browser identity logic.
benefits.prerequisites: Reviewed origin/credential policy and issuer behavior.
benefits.tradeoffs: CORS controls browser response access, not authorization; frontend guards remain presentation only.

checks: Credentialed requests succeed only for permitted origins.
Expired credentials transition to sign-in without endless retries.
Cross-tenant and CSRF probes are rejected by the backend.
transitions.rollback: Restore the old browser artifact/origin policy only if existing credential handling remains secure; retain revocation history.

transitions.existing_contract: Current fetch/cache behavior, stale tolerance, retry limits and account-switch isolation.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Introduce query keys for a bounded remote-state category; keep transient form state separate and compare outcomes with the old fetch path.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use explicit TanStack Query staleTime, retry, invalidation and account-clear policy where its remote-state cache serves a requirement.

benefits.benefit: Shared queries can reuse data and refresh deliberately.
benefits.prerequisites: A QueryClientProvider, stable tenant-aware keys and mutation invalidation.
benefits.tradeoffs: Default stale queries refetch on mount/focus/reconnect; retries can obscure application errors if left unspecified.

checks: A mutation refreshes affected list/detail views.
Switching accounts cannot reuse the old account's records.
Network restoration produces one coherent refresh; permission errors do not retry indefinitely.
transitions.rollback: Return the category to the old loader and clear the new cache; do not discard durable pending user operations.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing event envelope, authorization, IDs, reconnect behavior and replay/retention rules.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep a backend bridge producing the current event contract; move clients by stable subscription cohort rather than arbitrary per-request routing.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use EventSource for one-way events when host/credentials fit, WebSocket for bidirectional needs; persist/replay events separately when delivery requires it.

benefits.benefit: A standard browser event stream can replace bespoke polling for suitable feeds.
benefits.prerequisites: Authenticated endpoint, event IDs, retention/replay contract and streaming host.
benefits.tradeoffs: EventSource reconnect does not create server event history; its constructor has no arbitrary header option.

checks: Disconnect after event N and reconnect; no required event is omitted or applied twice.
Revocation terminates access and later reconnect is denied.
Old/new envelopes decode during mixed-version rollout.
transitions.rollback: Restore old polling/transport using the same cursor domain; reconcile delivered events and keep bridge/history through the rollback window.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing HTML/CDN/service-worker policy, lazy chunks and open-tab unsaved state.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep prior hashed assets and compatible APIs while serving new HTML to a cohort; include any existing service worker's activation/cache rules.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Revalidate HTML, retain old content-hashed chunks and handle vite:preloadError with a guarded refresh/update flow that preserves drafts.

benefits.benefit: Old tabs can continue loading their release's lazy chunks.
benefits.prerequisites: Asset retention, correct base path and tested update UX.
benefits.tradeoffs: Retention costs storage; refresh may lose state, and reload loops do not fix a wrong CDN policy.

checks: After deployment an old tab lazy-loads its old route successfully.
If a chunk is intentionally unavailable, the update path retains the draft and recovers once.
Production HTML/cache headers and API compatibility match the rollout policy.
transitions.rollback: Restore the prior HTML and retained assets, roll service-worker changes through their actual lifecycle, and keep new-client API support.

profiles.version_scope: Documentation reviewed 11 October 2026. SwiftUI Observation and SwiftData are iOS/iPadOS 17+; support older OS targets through compatible alternatives. Pin Xcode/SDK/Swift/package resolution and retain the minimum OS/device matrix. No simulator, archive or store-release check was executed.
profiles.operating_model: An installed iOS client persists across backend releases and is suspended or terminated under OS control. Recommendation: SwiftUI views render observable presentation state while repositories own URLSession DTOs and local persistence. Store rollout, API compatibility and local-store migration are separate adoption gates.
architecture: Use SwiftUI state/Observation according to minimum OS availability; keep view rendering separate from asynchronous repositories and business decisions. Observation is UI dependency tracking, not disk persistence.
Recommendation: version API DTOs separately from SwiftData/Core Data entities; preserve old installed-client contracts and authorize all privileged operations on the backend.

Use a versioned local schema and reviewed migration plan for SwiftData. Recommendation: store unacknowledged user intents durably before claiming an offline write succeeded; reconcile conflicts with an explicit server policy.
Separate foreground structured concurrency, OS-scheduled refresh/processing, background URLSession transfers and server durable jobs. Each has different completion and cancellation semantics.
Recommendation: Keychain stores credential material; isolate account-local data and clear/lock the appropriate state on account switch. Keep backend provider secrets out of the app bundle.
developer_workflow: Start in the external Xcode source checkout. Read README, minimum OS, shared scheme, signing owner, capabilities, API fixtures and every persisted schema version.

Record xcodebuild -version and xcode-select -p; use xcodebuild -list -project App.xcodeproj and xcodebuild -showdestinations -project App.xcodeproj -scheme App with the actual names. Resolve packages with xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies -project App.xcodeproj -scheme App. Check current flags with the pinned xcodebuild -help; the linked command-line FAQ is archived.

After choosing an installed simulator UUID, run xcodebuild test -project App.xcodeproj -scheme App -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=<UUID>' -resultBundlePath <new-path>.xcresult. Placeholders require substitution; simulator results do not establish device background behavior.

Recommendation: use Instruments/network diagnostics, physical-device background checks, upgrade fixtures, VoiceOver and large text. Produce a signed archive/TestFlight update under the established release workflow; record exact old/new client builds and compatible backend revisions.
avoid: Assuming users update when the backend deploys strands old installed clients and offline requests.
Assuming an older executable can read a migrated store confuses binary rollback with data rollback.
Keeping pending offline writes only in view state loses work after suspension or termination.
Using BGAppRefreshTask as an exact timer or unlimited durable worker ignores OS scheduling and expiration.
Using phased release as install reversal overlooks manual downloads and devices already running the new version.

transitions.existing_contract: Installed versions, minimum OS, URLSession DTOs/errors, deep links, auth expiry and old/offline writes.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Ship additive backend responses and versioned fixtures before the new client; retain old contracts until measured adoption and an explicit support policy permit retirement.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Separate API DTOs from local models and use capability negotiation for optional features; authorization remains backend-owned.

benefits.benefit: Independent backend/client deployment can preserve supported installations.
benefits.prerequisites: Inventory of real installed versions, API fixtures and release/support owners.
benefits.tradeoffs: Long-lived version support costs maintenance; a new store release cannot force immediate adoption.

checks: Old and new builds run against the same new backend.
Unknown optional fields and absent new fields do not break supported clients.
A delayed old-client mutation receives the documented success/conflict/upgrade response.
transitions.rollback: Disable the new server feature and retain both API contracts; already-installed clients require a compatible forward fix when needed.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing on-device store versions, entity meaning, relationships, pending local writes and upgrade paths.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Add compatible fields/stages before removing representations; migration fixtures include every supported historical store and unacknowledged operations.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use SwiftData VersionedSchema and SchemaMigrationPlan when OS support permits; preserve the established Core Data/store choice if migration value is unproven.

benefits.benefit: An explicit schema history makes upgrade behavior inspectable.
benefits.prerequisites: Reviewed stages and fixtures proving values/relationships/pending writes survive.
benefits.tradeoffs: Forward migration does not establish older-binary readability; cross-store conversion is application work.

checks: Open each supported old store with the new build and compare user data and pending operations.
Interrupt migration and verify recovery behavior.
Attempt the intended rollback build against the migrated fixture; reject release rollback if unreadable.
transitions.rollback: Prefer a compatible forward repair if downgrade is unqualified. Restore a pre-upgrade copy only under a reconciled policy that does not erase later local writes.

transitions.existing_contract: Local reads, pending offline changes, tombstones/cursors and server conflict semantics.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep the server as shared-domain reconciler; record each local mutation durably with a stable operation ID and schema version while old clients use the same conflict policy.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use repository-owned local reads and a persistent operation log when offline writes are required; choose revision checks, merge or user resolution per domain instead of accidental timestamp wins.

benefits.benefit: Users can retain local work through intermittent connectivity.
benefits.prerequisites: Durable local storage, replay-safe backend, explicit conflict/tombstone protocol.
benefits.tradeoffs: This is a proposed application design; SwiftData does not automatically provide arbitrary backend synchronization.

checks: Two devices edit the same record offline; the declared policy preserves or exposes both intents.
Disconnect after server commit but before acknowledgement; replay does not duplicate the effect.
Restart/sign-out does not silently replay account A operations as account B.
transitions.rollback: Stop the new synchronizer, retain pending operations and translate/reconcile them before returning to old logic; never clear the log as a rollback shortcut.

transitions.existing_contract: Foreground task cancellation, pending intents and any existing background task identifiers/handlers.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Retain old handler identifiers and persisted payload readers while new code is installed; use one owner per sync operation.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Choose BGAppRefreshTask/BGProcessingTask for eligible opportunistic device work, foreground tasks for interactive work and backend durable jobs for server completion obligations.

benefits.benefit: Eligible refresh/maintenance can execute while the app is backgrounded.
benefits.prerequisites: Capabilities, registered handlers, durable checkpoints and expiration handling.
benefits.tradeoffs: The OS selects launch time; device scheduling does not satisfy a fixed backend completion SLA.

checks: Expire a task midway; it checkpoints/cancels and marks completion correctly.
Suspend/terminate/relaunch and resume without a duplicated business effect.
Offline, battery and permission constraints show honest pending state.
transitions.rollback: Disable new task submission while preserving payload readers/handlers long enough to reconcile pending work; continue foreground sync or a server job where appropriate.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing upload/download IDs, authorized object keys, file hashes, task identifiers and completion acknowledgements.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Keep server upload endpoints/object ownership compatible; persist mapping from background task to logical operation and retain file-backed upload payloads.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use an identified background URLSession for eligible HTTP(S) transfer; recreate it after system termination and move completed temporary downloads before delegate return.

benefits.benefit: Transfers can continue during suspension without holding the app process.
benefits.prerequisites: Delegate lifecycle, stable session identifier, protected files and authorized retry/acknowledgement contract.
benefits.tradeoffs: Background uploads require files; scheduling is not exact and transfer completion differs from domain acceptance.

checks: Suspend during upload/download and restore the same session after system termination.
Verify file integrity and durable location after completion.
Retry an ambiguous response without producing duplicate owned objects.
transitions.rollback: Stop creating new transfers, inspect/cancel or finish existing tasks and reconcile server objects; keep session callbacks until all retained tasks are accounted for.

transitions.existing_contract: Store release ownership, supported devices, adoption, crash reports and persisted-data compatibility.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Verify TestFlight install-over-existing fixtures; retain server compatibility through phased adoption and include manual downloads in risk assessment.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use phased release with explicit crash/data-loss/compatibility stop criteria; assess adoption before retiring old API behavior.

benefits.benefit: Gradual automatic-update distribution can limit initial exposure.
benefits.prerequisites: Signed reviewed build, live telemetry and a compatible recovery release.
benefits.tradeoffs: Apple's seven-day phases cover eligible automatic updates; anyone can manually download, and pausing does not reverse installs.

checks: Verify real install/update preserves store, credentials and deep links.
Track old/new build support and migration failures separately.
Pause/recovery procedure leaves already-updated clients functional.
transitions.rollback: Pause further distribution and disable affected server capabilities if safe; ship a compatible repair rather than assuming an installed-version/store downgrade.

sources.claim: Swift Testing and XCTest/UI tests have complementary roles; testing is separate from distribution.

sources.claim: Documents command shapes for scheme/project/destination tests and archives; recheck options with the pinned Xcode toolchain.

profiles.version_scope: Documentation reviewed 11 October 2026. Use the project's minimum/target SDK, compatible Kotlin/Compose/AGP/Gradle/JDK/Room/WorkManager versions and version catalog. Current guidance is conditional on supported platform behavior; no APK, App Bundle, emulator or store release was tested.
profiles.operating_model: An installed Android client renders immutable screen state with lifecycle-aware collection and persists important data separately. Recommendation: repositories mediate Room/API data and WorkManager handles selected persistent work; backend services own privileged domain effects. Installed versions coexist through staged distribution.
architecture: Android guidance recommends separate UI and data layers, repositories, unidirectional data flow and lifecycle-aware Flow collection. Add a domain layer only when complexity/reuse warrants it.
Recommendation: keep API DTOs distinct from Room entities, and local observable data authoritative for offline screen reads while the backend owns shared-domain reconciliation.

Room owns schema versions and migrations; DataStore serves preferences rather than a general relational substitute. Record durable user operations and acknowledgement state when offline writes are required.
Coroutines serve lifecycle/in-process async work; WorkManager persists scheduled work across restart/reboot and remains subject to constraints and power policy.

Recommendation: use Keystore-backed keys to protect separately stored app-private credentials. A Keystore key is not arbitrary token storage, nor a guarantee that a revoked backend session remains usable.
developer_workflow: Start at the external source README, API and database fixtures, version catalog and Gradle wrapper. Record package identity, SDK/device matrix, signing owner and release track.
Use ./gradlew --version and ./gradlew tasks --all; with an actual app module run ./gradlew :app:lintDebug :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug. Keep wrapper/JDK/SDK inputs reproducible.

After adb devices identifies an authorized emulator/device, run ./gradlew :app:connectedDebugAndroidTest. Configure Room's migration testing/exported schemas; assertions must check preserved data as well as schema shape.

Recommendation: use Android Studio profilers/inspection, coroutine fakes, Compose navigation/accessibility tests and physical-device reboot/offline checks. Build ./gradlew :app:bundleRelease only with reviewed signing, then verify an internal-track install/update before staged promotion.
avoid: Collecting Flow without lifecycle ownership can keep work running when a screen is stopped; repeating effects inside recomposition can duplicate requests.
Treating a ViewModel or coroutine as disk persistence loses work on process death.
Using destructive migration for user-created offline data deletes the only copy.
Expecting WorkManager to execute at an exact wall-clock deadline ignores scheduling windows and power constraints.
Halt rollout is not uninstall or downgrade; already-updated users stay on the new build.

transitions.existing_contract: Supported installed APK versions/OS levels, DTOs/errors, auth, deep links and delayed old-client operations.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Deploy backward-compatible server behavior first; run old/new clients against it and retain contracts through explicit adoption/support gates.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Version API DTOs independently of Room entities and gate optional features by negotiated capability; keep backend authorization authoritative.

benefits.benefit: Client releases and backend changes can progress independently.
benefits.prerequisites: Installed-version inventory, shared API fixtures and support ownership.
benefits.tradeoffs: Maintaining old contracts costs work; Compose adoption does not upgrade installed clients.

checks: Old/new builds decode missing/unknown fields and documented errors.
A delayed old offline operation succeeds or returns the declared conflict.
Deep links, session expiry and denied resources work across supported releases.
transitions.rollback: Disable the new capability and preserve old/new APIs; repair already-installed clients with a compatible higher-version release when needed.

transitions.existing_contract: Room schema versions, exported schemas, all upgrade paths and user-owned unsynced records.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Add migrations without discarding old fields until adoption permits; include direct upgrades from every supported starting version.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Keep exported Room schemas and explicit migration tests; use automatic or manual migrations according to the actual change.

benefits.benefit: Reviewed migrations preserve local user data across updates.
benefits.prerequisites: Complete paths plus assertions on data/relationships/pending work.
benefits.tradeoffs: Schema validation alone does not establish value preservation; destructive fallback permanently deletes table data.

checks: MigrationTestHelper exercises each path and earliest-to-current upgrade.
Assert unsynced rows, IDs and relationships remain meaningful.
Verify intended downgrade behavior; prohibit destructive fallback for the only copy of user work.
transitions.rollback: Ship a forward repair when older code cannot read the new store; any restore requires reconciling writes made after upgrade.

transitions.existing_contract: Local source-of-truth reads, pending offline operations, revision/cursor/tombstone and conflict rules.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Use one repository and one reconciler for each data category; persist queued mutations with operation IDs before reporting success.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use Room-backed local reads and a durable operation queue when offline writes are needed; select push/pull/hybrid sync and a domain-specific conflict policy.

benefits.benefit: Cached local data can keep required reads available and preserve offline intent.
benefits.prerequisites: Server sync support, retry-safe writes and an explicit conflict policy.
benefits.tradeoffs: Offline-first reads do not imply offline writes; last-write-wins can discard intent and depends on metadata semantics.

checks: Two offline devices make conflicting changes and obtain the documented resolution.
Kill process after local commit and before network send; operation survives.
Repeat server-committed/unacknowledged mutation without duplication; honor deletes/tombstones.
transitions.rollback: Stop the new synchronizer and retain its queue; map remaining operations/cursors to old semantics before resume.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing queued Worker class names, input Data versions, unique-work identities and external effects.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Retain readers/worker entry points for already-enqueued payloads; transfer one job category and prevent duplicate schedulers.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use WorkManager for eligible persistent device work with constraints/backoff; keep server completion obligations in a backend durable job.

benefits.benefit: Scheduled work persists across restart and device reboot.
benefits.prerequisites: Compatible worker payloads, stable unique names, replay-safe effects and documented constraints.
benefits.tradeoffs: Scheduling windows/power policy affect timing; unique work does not provide exactly-once remote effects.

checks: Reboot with queued work and verify it resumes when constraints permit.
Update app with old queued input; the new worker decodes it.
Crash after remote effect/before acknowledgement and confirm retry is safe.
transitions.rollback: Cancel new scheduling and account for pending/running work; keep compatibility workers until drained or safely transformed.

transitions.existing_contract: Existing stored credential encryption, key alias/access constraints, backup exclusions, issuer expiry/revocation.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Retain the backend issuer and read old encrypted credential formats during a bounded transition; isolate account-local data.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use Keystore-backed cryptographic keys with reviewed encrypted app-private credential storage and backend revocation.

benefits.benefit: OS key protection can reduce key extraction exposure.
benefits.prerequisites: Qualified device/API support, key invalidation handling and a reviewed storage/backup policy.
benefits.tradeoffs: Keystore stores keys rather than arbitrary tokens; device protection does not replace backend authorization.

checks: Key invalidation produces a controlled sign-in path.
Backup/restore cannot silently expose unusable/plain credentials.
Sign-out/account switch stops old-account queued work and backend revocation is enforced.
transitions.rollback: Retain compatibility decryption only while secure; require sign-in if the old format/key cannot be restored safely.

transitions.existing_contract: Play tracks, signing/version codes, adoption, crash metrics and schema/API compatibility.
transitions.coexistence: Recommendation: Verify an internal/closed-track update over supported old builds and preserve compatible backend behavior for the whole mixed-version population.
transitions.target: Recommendation: Use a staged rollout with explicit crash/data-loss thresholds and a higher-version compatible repair path.

benefits.benefit: Percentage-based adoption can limit initial exposure.
benefits.prerequisites: Signed build, account/track owner, telemetry and recovery artifact.
benefits.tradeoffs: Halting only prevents further rollout; users who already updated remain on that version.

checks: Install-over-old-build retains unsynced data and auth.
Track failures by app/OS/schema version.
Halt/recovery rehearsal keeps already-updated users functional.
transitions.rollback: Halt additional rollout and disable the affected capability if safe; publish a compatible fixed build without assuming a downgrade of installed clients.

sources.title: Android Architecture Recommendations
sources.claim: Separate UI/data layers, repositories, immutable state and lifecycle-aware collection are documented recommendations.

sources.title: Android Offline-first Architecture
sources.claim: Local sources, queues, sync and conflict resolution need explicit policies; offline reads need not imply offline writes.

sources.title: Migrate Your Room Database
sources.claim: Migration testing should cover all paths; destructive fallback can permanently delete local table data.

sources.title: Android WorkManager Task Scheduling
sources.claim: Work is persisted and rescheduled across reboots with constraints/retries; it is not an exact timer or all immediate work.

sources.title: Android Keystore System
sources.claim: Keystore protects cryptographic key material and usage constraints; arbitrary credentials need their own protected storage design.

sources.title: Build Android Apps from the Command Line
sources.claim: Gradle wrapper build/test tasks and signed release artifacts require configured inputs.

sources.title: Play Console Staged Rollouts
sources.claim: Halting stops additional staged installs; already-updated users remain on that version.
